clue.text: Thief's initial motive for crime

indicators.note: initial asks for the opening letter of the word Thief's

parts.note: a motive is a reason for doing something

explanation.surface: A detective wonders what first drove a thief to break the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' takes T from 'Thief's'; REASON follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or sovereign is the gravest crime in law.

clue.text: Subjects run away from equate-rial regions

indicators.note: away from tells us one piece is taken out of the regions word

parts.note: the tropics are the regions either side of the equator
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Explorers' subjects flee the hot lands near the equator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' removes R (run, as on a cricket scorecard) from TROPICS. The clue's 'equate-rial' is the newspaper text's rendering of 'equatorial'.
explanation.definitionFit: Topics are the matters or themes under discussion, synonymous with subjects.

clue.text: Bonus is over the odds -super!

definitions.meaning: a bonus is something additional, given on top
over the odds means more than expected or necessary
super and the answer both work as prefixes or adjectives meaning especially big or fine

explanation.surface: Someone delighted at getting a payment above the expected rate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means additional, more than usual, and as a prefix or adjective very great, matching all three senses.

clue.text: The highest possible score is a treble

definitions.meaning: in a musical score the top voice part is the highest one
a treble is a boy singer with the highest range

explanation.surface: A sports fan boasts that a triple is the best result you can get.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' and 'treble' read as sporting terms (a darts treble, a match score) but both are musical here.
explanation.definitionFit: The top vocal part in choral music is sung by the highest voices, and a treble sings that same high line.

clue.text: Time for two back-to back numbers

parts.note: NO is the standard abbreviation for number

indicators.note: back-to back says the two numbers face each other, so the second one is turned round

parts.note: the second of the two numbers is again NO

explanation.surface: A clock reading shows two digits standing back to back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two ... numbers' gives NO twice; 'back-to back' turns the second to ON, so the pair reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is a specific time on the clock, twelve o'clock.

clue.text: Men in ship producing props

indicators.note: in puts the men inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a crew is the men who work a ship

explanation.surface: Sailors aboard a vessel are making stage props.
explanation.walkthrough: 'props' looks like theatrical properties but means propellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships' screws are their propellers, often shortened to props.

clue.text: Something easily overlooked is small shopping area font

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a mall is a shopping precinct
a font is a typeface, i.e. print

explanation.surface: A tiny typeface used in a mall's signage goes unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract terms in tiny type are notoriously missed by readers who skim.

clue.text: What I'd give for lolly? Extraordinary price with heartless type

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests the letters are put into an unusual order
heartless means the middle of the word type is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A shopper complains of a strange price for an ice lolly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves TE from 'type'; 'Extraordinary' rearranges PRICE with TE. Lolly is British slang for money, as well as an ice lolly.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper hands over a written acknowledgement of payment when given cash.

clue.text: Cuff winds Bart in a bad way

indicators.note: in a bad way suggests the letters are disordered and damaged

explanation.surface: Someone named Bart is left winded and in poor shape by a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuff' suggests a blow, but it is the band round the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuff is a band of fabric encircling the wrist, as is this strip.

clue.text: What to do with this lot!

definitions.text: What to do with this lot!

parts.words: What to do with this lot!
parts.note: a lot is an item offered at a saleroom, so the advice is to send it under the hammer; the surface sounds like exasperation at a pile of stuff

explanation.surface: Someone exasperated at a heap of clutter asks what to do with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Items at a saleroom are lots, and they are offered for sale to bidders.

clue.text: Cradles for sisters, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to cradle is to hold tenderly or tend, like a carer holding a baby
a sister is a senior hospital carer, one example

explanation.surface: Siblings might be given cots for babies.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a baby is to hold it gently, and ward sisters are senior medical carers.

clue.text: Jazz fan has endless praise for neckwear

indicators.note: has means the fan holds the next piece within it

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the praise word is cut off

parts.note: to rave is to praise enthusiastically

explanation.surface: A jazz lover heaps praise on a neck accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the praise word to RAV, and 'has' means the jazz fan holds it. Cat for a jazz lover is dated slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a wide scarf-like tie worn around the neck.

clue.text: Arcade could be costlier

indicators.note: could be hints that the letters of the word may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A shopping arcade might turn out pricier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arcade' looks like a shopping arcade, but it is a covered walkway with arches.
explanation.definitionFit: A covered colonnaded walk round a monastery courtyard is a series of arches.

clue.text: Overcome by fun, decline getting drunk

indicators.note: getting drunk says the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Partygoers lose their resistance and start drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To be swayed or prevailed upon is to be overcome, as by drink.

clue.text: A glass vessel

definitions.meaning: a tall glass used for sherry or beer
a sailing ship with fore-and-aft rigging

explanation.surface: A drinking glass, or container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' reads as a container like the glass, but it is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a large sherry or beer glass and a two-masted sailing ship.

clue.text: Go in after fish and chips

indicators.note: after places the go-in piece behind the fish

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to go in is to enter

explanation.surface: Ordering fish and chips at a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish and chips' reads as a meal, but 'chips' is the definition: Chips is a traditional British nickname for a carpenter, who chips wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips is a long-standing nickname for a woodworker, especially a ship's joiner.

clue.text: Diatribe I dropped for business

indicators.note: dropped says a letter is let fall from the word

parts.note: a diatribe is a tirade, a bitter verbal attack

explanation.surface: A rant is abandoned in favour of commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of TIRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade is commerce, the buying and selling that makes up business.

clue.text: Be quiet and safe on the way!

definitions.meaning: an informal command to shut up
fastening a seatbelt keeps a passenger safe on a journey

explanation.surface: A driving instructor tells a pupil to hush and stay safe.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for shut up and also means fasten one's seatbelt in a car.

clue.text: Starting off panic is a mistake

indicators.note: starting off says the first letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: terror is extreme fear, panic

explanation.surface: Beginning to panic leads to a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a slip, a fault or a blunder.

clue.text: Comes to a conclusion about anxieties

parts.note: re means about, concerning
aches are pangs of worry or longing

explanation.surface: Someone arrives at a decision regarding their worries.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at an end point or destination is to get as far as it.

clue.text: Letter giving pension rights?

parts.note: a letter is one who lets rooms, and a pension is a boarding house, so this is someone letting lodgings, not a written letter about retirement income

explanation.surface: A written notice granting someone retirement benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who lets rooms in a boarding house to lodgers runs the property.

clue.text: Gentle child left with family under a doctor

indicators.note: under places the family below the doctor in this down clue

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A mild-mannered child is left in a doctor's care with relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A little lamb is a term of endearment for a meek, tender youngster.

clue.text: Dismiss the start of test on the French badger

indicators.note: dismiss the start of means drop the opening letter of the test word

parts.note: to check is to test
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: A French badger is sent away at the start of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dismiss the start of' trims the test word to HECK; 'on' means it sits above the French article in a down entry. 'badger' is the verb, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester them, as an interrupter does a speaker.

clue.text: I generate mess?

indicators.note: mess signals that the letters are jumbled into disorder

explanation.surface: A self-aware youngster admits to making a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is spoken by an untidy adolescent, and also says that GENERATE in a mess makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescents are stereotypically blamed for untidy bedrooms, so the clue is their confession.

clue.text: Spike Sprite with alcoholic drink

parts.note: a sprite is a mischievous fairy, an imp
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Someone laces a lemonade with booze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' and 'Sprite' suggest lacing a soft drink, but Sprite is a fairy and spike means pierce.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce or run through with a pointed stake.

clue.text: Marble in a doorway

parts.note: a gate is an entrance or doorway

explanation.surface: A marble is found at an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marble' suggests stone, but here it is a children's glass or stone marble, often made of agate.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded semi-precious stone used to make playing marbles, which are called agates.

clue.text: Stud's manager

definitions.meaning: a stud is a raised ornamental knob; the 's stands for is
a manager is the person in charge

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of a horse-breeding farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stud' suggests a horse farm, but it is a decorative raised knob.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a raised round ornament on a shield and the person in charge at work.

clue.text: Correct position of hands during fall?

definitions.text: Correct position of hands during fall?

parts.words: Correct position of hands during fall?
parts.note: the hands are those on a dial, and fall is the American autumn, when daylight saving ends and dials go back an hour

explanation.surface: Advice on how to hold your arms when tumbling over.
explanation.definitionFit: When summer time ends in autumn, timepieces are reset one hour earlier.

clue.text: Journalist, after a long time succeeded in being struck off

indicators.note: after places the journalist behind the other pieces

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter, after years of service, finally got removed from the register.
explanation.definitionFit: Being struck off a list means being deleted or removed from it.

clue.text: Frank is for keeping the Queen

indicators.note: keeping says the first word holds the Queen inside it

parts.note: for and since both mean because
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Frank is in charge of looking after the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name, but it means honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank means candid and honest, sincere in speech.
